A_target.statement: The three [[Definition:Median of Triangle|medians]] of a [[Definition:Triangle (Geometry)|triangle]] $\triangle ABC$ are [[Definition:Concurrent Lines|concurrent]] at a point $G$ dividing each median in the ratio $2 : 1$ from the vertex.

B_source.statement:
In a [[Definition:Vector Space|vector space]], the point dividing the segment from $\mathbf p$ to $\mathbf q$ in the ratio $\lambda : \paren {1 - \lambda}$ is:
:$\paren {1 - \lambda} \mathbf p + \lambda \mathbf q$

derived.the symmetric combination (a + b + c)/3: the common point of the medians

object_map.reformulation: Transport the incidence statement into vector algebra, where the candidate point is visibly symmetric in the vertices.

validity_conditions: The argument only uses affine combinations, so it holds in any dimension.
Division by 2 and 3 is needed, so over a general field the characteristic must not be 2 or 3.
proof_plan:
Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$, $\mathbf c$ be the position vectors of $A$, $B$, $C$.
The midpoint of $BC$ is $\mathbf m_a = \dfrac {\mathbf b + \mathbf c} 2$.

By the source result with $\lambda = \dfrac 2 3$, the point two thirds of the way from $A$ to $\mathbf m_a$ is:
:$\dfrac 1 3 \mathbf a + \dfrac 2 3 \mathbf m_a = \dfrac {\mathbf a + \mathbf b + \mathbf c} 3$
This expression is symmetric in $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$, $\mathbf c$, so the same point lies two thirds of the way along each median.

Hence the medians meet at the [[Definition:Centroid of Triangle|centroid]] $G = \dfrac {\mathbf a + \mathbf b + \mathbf c} 3$, which divides each in the ratio $2 : 1$.
{{qed}}
